name: PEASS-ng
section: Highlights
description: Windows and Linux privilege-escalation suites (winPEAS, linPEAS): thousands of checks over services, paths, credentials and scheduled tasks. Used by pentesters sweeping for escalation paths; the de-facto standard priv-escalation audit on every engagement. (GPL-2.0-or-later)

name: Evil-WinRM
section: Highlights
description: The ultimate WinRM shell: PS history, tab completion, pass-the-hash logins, LAPS download and file exchange over WinRM/SMB. Used by pentesters who hold credentials and want the fastest route to an interactive shell; the WinRM shell every AD course teaches. (LGPL-3.0)

name: Ligolo-ng
section: Highlights
description: Reverse socks5 tunneling for pivots: one TUN interface maps the agent's networks into your local routing table, no proxychains juggling. Used by red-teamers pivoting through internal ranges; the tunnel that made pivoting feel local. (GPL-3.0)

name: Rubeus
section: Highlights
description: Kerberos interaction toolkit: AS-REP roasting, kerberoasting, pass-the-key, delegation abuse and diamond-ticket crafting. Used by AD attackers working the Kerberos layer; the GhostPack Kerberos swiss-army knife. (BSD-3-Clause)

name: CUPP
section: Highlights
description: Common User Passwords Profiler: generates targeted wordlists from a victim's biography — names, dates, hobbies, languages. Used by pentesters crafting personalized wordlists; the original target-specific wordlist generator. (GPL-3.0)

name: GoMapEnum
section: Highlights
description: User enumeration and password spraying across SMB, Kerberos, NTLM and LDAP from a single Go binary. Used by red-teamers enumerating Windows users before a spray; the Go-native Windows enum-and-spray chain. (GPL-3.0)

name: Legba
section: Highlights
description: Multiprotocol brute-forcer — SSH, FTP, SMTP, HTTP, MySQL, MSSQL, Redis and more — with one consistent CLI. Used by pentesters who want a single cracker for every protocol; evilsocket's answer to scattered brute-forcers. (GPL-3.0)

name: DonPAPI
section: Highlights
description: Remote DPAPI credential collection: Chrome cookies, Wi-Fi keys and custom DPAPI blobs gathered from many hosts without touching disk. Used by attackers chaining credentials across Windows estates; the remote DPAPI collector that opens every browser. (GPL-3.0)

name: Certify
section: Highlights
description: Active Directory Certificate Services abuse toolkit: finds vulnerable certificate templates and chains ESC1-ESC8 from misconfigured CAs to domain compromise. Used by AD attackers auditing certificate services; the GhostPack tool that made AD CS a standard attack class. (BSD-3-Clause)

name: airgeddon
section: Highlights
description: All-in-one wireless security suite: handshakes, evil-twin attacks, captive portals, WPS and pmkid workflows behind one interactive menu. Used by Wi-Fi auditors running the full wireless chain; the menu-driven Wi-Fi lab. (GPL-3.0)

name: SMBMap
section: Highlights
description: SMB enumeration and share mapping: lists drives, permissions and writable shares, then downloads across a whole subnet. Used by pentesters enumerating Windows shares; the share-mapping staple since 2015. (GPL-3.0)

name: Medusa
section: Highlights
description: Parallel login brute-forcer for many services with modular credential lists and host batching. Used by pentesters running credential attacks at scale; the speed-first login cracker of the THC-Hydra era. (GPL-2.0)

name: Penelope
section: Highlights
description: Automated shell handler: catches reverse shells, upgrades them to fully interactive TTYs and logs every session. Used by pentesters tired of stty-raw gymnastics; the shell upgrader that saves the first ten minutes of every engagement. (GPL-3.0)

name: Pacu
section: Highlights
description: AWS exploitation framework: enumerates an account's services and chains misconfigurations into privilege-escalation paths. Used by cloud attackers chaining AWS misconfigs; the RhinoSecurity toolkit that defined open AWS offense. (BSD-3-Clause)

name: nomore403
section: Highlights
description: 403/401 bypass toolkit: path-normalization tricks, header fuzzing and method overrides that turn forbidden pages into accessible ones. Used by bug hunters probing access-control edges; the 403-bypass playbook codified. (MIT)

name: gotestwaf
section: Highlights
description: WAF assessment harness: fires ~900 benign-and-attack test cases (OWASP, fauxpas, shadowd) at a protected path and grades what the WAF actually blocks, with a hardening report. Used by pentesters measuring WAF effectiveness before tuning payloads; the Wallarm WAF benchmark. (MIT)

name: cvcemap
section: Highlights
description: ProjectDiscovery's CVE-to-version mapping (repo: vulnx): fingerprint a component and get the live CVE list for the exact version in one command. Used by recon pipelines mapping component exposure; the projectdiscovery take on CVE mapping. (MIT)

name: tlsx
section: Highlights
description: TLS-focused recon: cipher and certificate enumeration, SAN extraction and TLS-version probing with the projectdiscovery CLI ergonomics. Used by recon pipelines snapshotting TLS posture; the fast TLS recon companion. (MIT)

name: cdncheck
section: Highlights
description: Detects whether a host sits behind a CDN or known cloud provider before you scan it, from ProjectDiscovery's curated provider list. Used by recon pipelines avoiding wasted scans on protected edges; the suite's CDN gatekeeper. (MIT)

name: findomain
section: Highlights
description: Subdomain discovery through certificate transparency and multiple data sources with a database backend. Used by bug hunters building subdomain inventories; one of the fastest passive enumerators of its generation. (GPL-3.0)

name: knockpy
section: Highlights
description: Subdomain enumeration by wordlist and CT logs with wildcard detection built in. Used by pentesters running dictionary subdomain passes; the classic knock turned into a maintained Python tool. (GPL-3.0)

name: subcat
section: Highlights
description: Subdomain discovery through search-engine and passive sources, built for pipeline use. Used by recon chains wanting passive subdomain sets; the lightweight passive-enum addition. (MIT)

name: graphw00f
section: Highlights
description: GraphQL fingerprinter: detects the engine behind an endpoint — Apollo, Hasura, Yoga and the rest — from behavioral signatures. Used by pentesters preparing engine-specific GraphQL payloads; the fingerprinter that tells you which GraphQL you are attacking. (BSD-3-Clause)

name: graphinder
section: Highlights
description: GraphQL endpoint discovery: expands domains from CT logs and certificate SANs, then probes permutations with a wordlist to find unlisted GraphQL endpoints. Used by bug bounty hunters hunting hidden GraphQL surfaces; Escape Technologies' dockerized finder that pairs with graphw00f. (MIT)

name: gowitness
section: Highlights
description: Website screenshot recon: headless Chrome captures whole asset inventories and serves them in a browsable report. Used by bug hunters eyeballing thousands of hosts at once; the recon screenshot standard. (GPL-3.0)

name: FAVIHUNTER
section: Highlights
description: Favicon-based asset hunting: mmh3 favicon hashes match your targets' properties against public scan datasets. Used by attack-surface mappers looking for forgotten properties; the favicon-hash bridge for asset discovery. (MIT)

name: gitjacker
section: Highlights
description: Leaks .git directories from misconfigured webservers and reconstructs the repository history. Used by bug hunters checking for exposed source; the git-dump attack automated. (Unlicense)

name: InfoHound
section: Highlights
description: OSINT search-engine framework: crawls people, emails, domains and leaks into structured intelligence reports. Used by investigators building target dossiers; the i2CAT open intelligence engine. (AGPL-3.0)

name: Investigo
section: Highlights
description: Username and email finder across social networks and forums with a clean CLI. Used by OSINT researchers tracing identities; a long-standing social presence mapper. (MIT)

name: EmailHarvester
section: Highlights
description: Email enumeration via search engines and public sources. Used by OSINT collectors gathering corporate footprints; the maldevel classic that keeps earning its place. (GPL-3.0)

name: Instaloader
section: Highlights
description: Instagram archiving: photos, stories, captions and metadata downloaded rate-limit-aware. Used by investigators archiving social evidence; the Instagram archiver that respects both public data and platform limits. (MIT)

name: gallery-dl
section: Highlights
description: Command-line downloader for image galleries and video collections from hundreds of sites, for authorized archiving and OSINT work. Used by archivers preserving online media; the gallery downloader that covers almost every platform. (GPL-2.0)

name: TestDisk
section: Highlights
description: Partition-table and file recovery: undeletes, fixes boot sectors and rescues lost partitions across most filesystems. Used by DFIR and ops teams rescuing broken disks; the cgsecurity recovery classic. (GPL-2.0)

name: androguard
section: Highlights
description: Reverse-engineering framework for Android: DEX/ODEX parsing, decompilation, static analysis and APK diffing in Python. Used by mobile analysts tearing APKs apart; the Android RE foundation. (Apache-2.0)

name: hurl
section: Highlights
description: HTTP requests in plain text: run and test endpoints with a human-readable format, assertions and CI-ready reports. Used by API testers scripting endpoint checks; the plain-text HTTP runner. (Apache-2.0)

name: chisel
section: Highlights
description: TCP tunnel over HTTP: a single client/server binary pairs port-forwards through restrictive egress. Used by red-teamers tunneling through web-exit-only networks; the jpillora tunnel standard. (MIT)

name: GoReplay
section: Highlights
description: Traffic replay: capture production HTTP and replay it at scale against staging — shadow testing with real load instead of synthetic. Used by testers replaying real traffic; the open-core replay standard. (LGPL-3.0, open-core)

name: Slither
section: Highlights
description: Solidity static analysis: 90+ detectors for reentrancy, variable shadowing and dangerous patterns in smart contracts. Used by auditors reviewing Solidity; the smart-contract SAST standard. (AGPL-3.0)

name: AFL++
section: Highlights
description: The fuzzer: coverage-guided mutation with modern instrumentation for everything from parsers to kernels. Used by researchers finding memory corruption; the community fuzzer that keeps out-performing the original AFL. (AGPL-3.0)

name: pip-audit
section: Highlights
description: Scans Python environments for known vulnerabilities against the PyPA advisory database. Used by Python shops securing their dependency trees; the official PyPA audit tool. (Apache-2.0)

name: xeol
section: Highlights
description: End-of-life dependency detection: finds packages past their support lifetime in SBOMs and repositories. Used by DevSecOps teams tracking EOL software; the lifecycle-aware scanner. (Apache-2.0)

name: CodeQL
section: Highlights
description: Semantic code analysis from GitHub: query code as a database and hunt vulnerability classes across languages with variant analysis. Used by security researchers hunting bug classes at scale; free for open-source research. (MIT)

name: cloudfox
section: Highlights
description: Cloud attack-surface auditor: maps IAM, services and privileges across AWS, Azure and GCP for engagement prep. Used by cloud pentesters building their attack map; the BishopFox cloud 'who am I' reconnaissance tool. (MIT)

name: GCP Scanner
section: Highlights
description: Google Cloud security scanner: enumerates projects, services, IAM and exposure across a GCP organization. Used by cloud auditors assessing GCP estates; the official google/gcp_scanner. (Apache-2.0)

name: Tracee
section: Highlights
description: Container runtime security tracing with eBPF: follows syscalls and events to detect suspicious behavior in real time. Used by runtime-security teams watching containers live; Aquasecurity's eBPF sensor. (Apache-2.0)

name: Hayabusa
section: Highlights
description: Windows event-log analysis and threat hunting: parses EVTX at speed, detects with built-in Sigma rules and builds timelines. Used by DFIR hunters triaging Windows estates; the Yamato-Security log analyzer. (AGPL-3.0)

name: Netlas
section: Highlights
description: Internet-registry search across ASNs, DNS, certificates and network data with a generous free tier for researchers. Used by OSINT and attack-surface work at zero budget; the registry search with the free-research tier. (free tier)

name: Metasploit Framework
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: The world's most-used pentest framework; thousands of validated modules for exploitation, post-engagement evidence gathering and reporting in authorized tests. Used by professional penetration testers and red teams in authorized engagements; the open-source counterpart to commercial exploitation platforms like Core Impact and Cobalt Strike.

name: Nmap
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

Used by bug bounty hunters and enterprise security teams alike for template-driven scanning at scale; a free staple that rivals paid web-scanning engines for public attack-surface checks.

name: afrog
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Fast cross-platform vulnerability scanner driven by a 1,700+ community-maintained YAML PoC corpus covering CVE, CNVD, unauthorized-access, default-password and fingerprinting checks. Used by bug bounty hunters and pentesters running corpus-driven scans; the open-source scanner with one of the largest community PoC collections. (MIT)

name: OWASP ZAP
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

Used by web pentesters who want a full proxy workbench without a license; the open alternative built on the ZAP engine.. (AGPL-3.0)

name: hetty
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: HTTP toolkit for security research: an intercepting proxy with scope rules, request composer and replay, and a GraphQL management API in one self-hosted Go binary. name: Akto
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

Used by API security teams testing business-logic flaws generic DAST misses; the open-source alternative to API-scanning SaaS. (MIT)

name: sqlmap
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: The definitive SQL injection detection and exploitation tool for authorized web application testing. Used by penetration testers everywhere for SQL injection proof; the definitive free SQLi automation tool with no real commercial equal. (GPL-2.0)

name: unKover
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: The 403 access-bypass tester: a 13-technique battery (path rewrites, header tricks, HTTP method and version shifts) that turns forbidden endpoints into authorized access. Used by web pentesters proving 403s are misconfigurations during engagements; the focused free alternative to commercial authz-testing modules. (MIT per README)

name: jwt-hack
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: JWT attack toolkit: cracking, payload generation, alg-confusion and claim-abuse checks for JSON Web Tokens in one CLI. Used by bug bounty hunters and pentesters auditing token-based authentication; the dedicated free toolkit for the JWT bug class.. (MIT)

name: Impacket
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: The standard Python library for low-level Windows protocol work (SMB, LDAP, Kerberos); powers wmiexec/secretsdump-class tooling and AD assessments. Used by red teamers and AD security researchers; the Python underpinning of countless offensive and defensive toolkits.

name: MITRE Caldera
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Scalable adversary-emulation platform built on ATT&CK; run purple-team exercises that prove your detections actually fire. Used by red teams and purple teams for automated adversary emulation; the open-source alternative to commercial breach-attack-simulation platforms like AttackIQ and SafeBreach.

name: Realm
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Open-source adversary-emulation framework with cross-platform implants and Terraform-driven C2 infrastructure for authorized red teams. Used by red teams running repeatable, scoped adversary emulation; the open-source alternative to commercial adversary-simulation platforms. (GPL-3.0)

name: BloodHound
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

name: MobSF
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: All-in-one mobile app security: static + dynamic analysis for Android/iOS in a single pipeline. Used by mobile app security testers for static and dynamic analysis; the open-source alternative to commercial mobile app testing suites. (GPL-3.0)

name: WPScan
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Black-box WordPress scanner: plugin/theme enumeration and version-based vuln lookups. Used by WordPress security auditors and managed-service providers; the standard black-box WordPress scanner, free alternative to paid WP security suites. (free for non-commercial use)

name: Bettercap
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: The Swiss-army knife for authorized network assessments: ARP/DNS spoofing, MITM proxies, WiFi and BLE modules. Used by network penetration testers for authorized MITM analysis; the modern successor to Ettercap in most toolkits. (GPL-3.0)

name: Nikto
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Venerable web-server scanner; noisy but thorough on server misconfigurations and default files. Used by web server auditors for two decades; the venerable free complement to commercial web scanners' misconfiguration checks. (GPL-3.0; DB files have custom terms)

name: h5i
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Agent-native web-security workspace: deterministic recon, secrets scanning, DOM post-message auditing and CI regression checks — fully usable without any LLM key. Used by security engineers wanting agent-native, deterministic web checks; a newer open alternative to dashboard-driven commercial scanners. (Apache-2.0)

name: goshs
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Hardened HTTP file-transfer server built for engagements: upload/download, authentication, access control and TLS — the modern replacement for `python -m http.server`. Used by pentesters on engagements as a hardened file-transfer server; the security-hardened alternative to spinning up ad-hoc Python servers.

name: Dalfox
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Fast XSS scanner with DOM-aware analysis and a strong payload set; the modern XSS go-to. Used by bug bounty hunters for fast, DOM-aware XSS scanning; a favorite free alternative to Burp's scanner for XSS-only sweeps.

name: pphack
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Advanced client-side prototype-pollution scanner for JavaScript-heavy web apps. Used by bug bounty hunters auditing front-end pollution sinks; the dedicated free scanner for this bug class. (MIT)

name: NetExec
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: CrackMapExec's actively maintained successor; audit credential hygiene and service misconfigurations across whole subnets. Used by internal network auditors and AD pentesters for credential-hygiene sweeps.

name: Responder
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: LLMNR/NBT-NS/MDNS poisoner; the fastest way to demonstrate credential-leak exposure on an authorized internal network. Used by internal penetration testers to demonstrate credential exposure on enterprise networks; the canonical LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoner. (GPL-3.0)

section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

Used by teams wiring delivery-grade SQLi detection into CI pipelines; the automation-first SQLi scanner that complements sqlmap. (MIT)

name: NoSQLMap
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: NoSQL injection testing for MongoDB, CouchDB and Redis-backed apps: injection, enumeration and data extraction for document-store backends. Used by pentesters attacking NoSQL endpoints where SQLi tooling does not apply; the reference NoSQL injection toolkit since 2013. (GPL-3.0)

name: 2MNY Website Vulnerability Scanner
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Open-source web vulnerability scanner with 202 deterministic modules: OWASP Top 10, XSS/SQLi/SSRF, subdomain takeover, WordPress and AI/LLM surface checks, CVSS-scored evidence and HTML/PDF reports. Self-hosted via Docker. Used by security teams that want evidence-backed, deterministic scanning they can self-host; the open-source alternative to paid scanner SaaS for website attack surfaces. (maintainer's project)

name: masscan
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

name: Tsunami
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

name: Prism X

name: SoliTools
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

name: Hakscan
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
description: Fast, self-contained vulnerability scanner shipped as a single Go binary — covers web apps, APKs and binaries, extensible with JSON and nuclei YAML templates. Used by bug bounty hunters wanting one-binary scanning across target types; the portable free scanner for quick triage.. (MIT)

name: nemesis
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools

name: wafw00f
section: ⚔️ The Armory — Offensive Security, Pentesting & Bug Bounty Tools
